newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 falls led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 falls led by blue chips.

text.p: Czech shares continued to edge lower on Wednesday with the PX50 index falling 0.9 points to 571.9 led mainly by blue chip issues.

The biggest loser among the major issues was Komercni Banka which shed 30 crowns to 2,340. Meanwhile, savings bank Ceska Sporitelna, the only high cap gainer, rose eight crowns to 367 putting it just three crowns below its 12-month high.
SPT Telecom lost 15 crowns to 3,345 and CEZ was down three crowns to 1,045.

On Wednesday morning, the Czech Statistical Office released data showing a slowdown in gross domestic product growth in the second quarter of 1996 to just four percent from 4.6 percent in the first quarter.
The figures were below general expectations but equity dealers expected the stock exchange to be virtually unaffected.
"The figure was not so far below expectations. I don't expect a...significant impact on the equity market," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.
